posts.heading: October 28, 2026
posts.text:
The day's 26 species was the most of the eight days, matching October 25, and its 201 visits sat close to the week's average of 202.0. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 64, followed by Carolina Wren with 32 and Carolina Chickadee with 24. Heard detections totaled 326, below the week's average of 378.4, with Eastern Towhee leading at 53.

Fourteen species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Blue Jay, Northern Cardinal, Song Sparrow, and Tufted Titmouse. Eastern Screech-Owl was recorded on six of the seven days, including this one. Red-shouldered Hawk was recorded on each of the previous seven days but not today. Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned after 16 days away, last recorded on October 12.

The audio source changed many times through the day, so the heard total draws on more than one microphone. No species was seen or heard for the first time at this station. One highlight was a Blue Jay that perched on the water bowl's rim, bent to drink, and flew off.

posts.heading: October 27, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday was quieter than the week before at this station, with 117 feeder visits against a seven-day average of 212.4 and 19 species against an average of 22.6. Heard detections, at 377, sat close to the average of 390.4, so the drop was mostly in visits. Fifteen species were recorded on each of the last seven days, including this one, and the regulars held, with Eastern Towhee, White-throated Sparrow, Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinal all heard across the whole week.

Brown Thrasher returned after 8 days away, last recorded on 2026-10-19, and was seen once as a probable visit. Eastern Screech-Owl was seen once and has been recorded on 5 of the last 7 days. Canada Goose and Mourning Dove were recorded on 5 of the last 7 days but not yesterday, and no species was heard for the first time at this station.

The audio source was switched repeatedly through the day between the pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1) and c120 units, so the heard counts came from more than one microphone.

posts.heading: October 26, 2026
posts.text:
October 26 added up to 173 feeder visits across 22 species, with 19 species heard and 12 seen, 9 of them both. That is quieter than the past week's average of 214.9 visits, though the species count matched the average of 22.1. Tufted Titmouse led the day with 62 confident visits, and Eastern Towhee was the most heard species at 60 detections. Every species recorded on this day was also recorded on each of the previous seven days, except for the Eastern Meadowlark, which returned after 10 days away with its last detection on October 16.

The station's audio source was switched many times between c120, pi, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) across the week, with frequent changes on October 26 itself. The week's heard totals ranged from 312 to 461 per day, and today's 368 sits near the middle of that range.

The last visual of the day was an Eastern Screech-Owl, recorded as probable, 948 minutes after sunrise.
